subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)
content:
From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

Hi Naomi,

We’re finalizing the cross-SDK auth standard (Python/TS/Go) as part of the parity audit. Could Security do a quick review for secure defaults + redaction?

Draft attached: SDK-Auth-Standard-DRAFT-v3.md

Key points (proposed):
- API key resolution order: explicit param > env var > (optional) config file
- Env var names: REDWOOD_API_KEY (primary), REDWOOD_TOKEN (alias)
- Header: Authorization: Bearer <key>
- Errors: clear remediation, no secret echoing
- Logging: redact Authorization and any header keys containing “key”, “token”, “authorization”

We’re trying to close SUP-9355 (auth error messaging unclear when env var missing) without introducing key leakage.

If you can, please respond with approval conditions by EOW so we can land changes in the SDK PRs.

Thanks,
Ibrahim
Tech Lead, SDKs
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

Thanks Ibrahim.

A few questions/concerns before we sign off:

1) Config file support: do we actually need it? If yes, must be opt-in and must not expand the default “secret search path” without clear docs. Keys in developer home dirs have caused incident postmortems in other orgs.

2) Env var names: we should pick ONE canonical name for docs and error messages. Aliases are okay but can create ambiguity during enterprise reviews (“which one is used?”).

3) Redaction scope: please ensure we also redact in:
- debug logs
- thrown exceptions (e.g., request dump helpers)
- retry instrumentation hooks

4) Error message copy: we can be explicit without being overly verbose. Something like “Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass apiKey explicitly. See <docs>.” Avoid printing the value or the first/last chars.

5) For multi-tenant apps, we need guidance that keys must be tenant-scoped and never logged; do we have a section that’s clear?

Kevin can you take first pass on the diffs and call out any risky patterns? I’ll do the spec pass once those are addressed.

- Naomi
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 8:26 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

I reviewed the Python + TS diffs.

Findings / requested changes:

A) Config file
- Python patch has a TODO for reading ~/.config/redwood/key. This should not ship as a default search path. If we keep it, it must be explicitly enabled (e.g., enableConfigFileLookup=true) and it must use a single, documented file location.

B) Logging / error objects
- TS diff currently passes “headers” through the error object in one path (when building a request debug string). That object will include Authorization in some runtimes.
  - Fix: ensure Authorization is removed before constructing any error/debug output.

C) Redaction rules
- Recommend a shared helper in each SDK: redactSecrets(map<string,string>) where the matcher is case-insensitive and matches:
  - authorization
  - *api-key*
  - *token*
  - x-redwood-*
- Also redact query params if we ever allow apiKey in query (we shouldn’t).

D) Canonical env var
- Agree with Naomi: pick REDWOOD_API_KEY as the canonical name in docs/errors. Alias acceptable but should not appear in docs as “either/or”.

No blockers beyond the above if we implement the fixes and add at least one unit test per SDK proving “Authorization never appears in exception messages.”

Kevin
Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 2:14 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

All makes sense. Proposed updates (we can implement in all SDKs):

1) Config file lookup
- We’ll remove config file lookup from the default resolution order.
- If we keep it at all, it will be behind an explicit opt-in flag and documented as “advanced / not recommended for production.” (We can also punt it entirely for v1.)

2) Canonical env var
- Docs + error messages will reference only REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- We’ll keep REDWOOD_TOKEN as a backward-compatible alias but not mention it in quickstarts.

3) Redaction
- Add redactSecrets() helper per SDK and run it on:
  - any request/response headers included in errors
  - any debug logging hooks (when enabled)
  - telemetry hooks (retry/timeout instrumentation)

4) Error message copy
- “Missing API key. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY or pass apiKey. Docs: <link>”
- No truncation/partial display of key.

5) Tests
- Add a regression test in conformance harness and per-SDK unit tests verifying Authorization is never present in thrown error strings.

Naomi/Aisha: once we push these changes into the draft spec and update the diffs, can we get conditional approval to proceed with the PRs?

Ibrahim

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim.khan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 10:48 AM
Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

Adding one more approval condition from my side:

- “Safe by default” must be true across language runtimes.
  - TS: avoid relying on console.debug conventions; ensure SDK does not log headers unless the caller explicitly turns on debug logging.
  - Go/Python: same; no implicit request dumping.

Also please ensure we don’t include tenant identifiers + Authorization in the same log line (common correlation mistake).

If the above is met + Kevin’s list is addressed, I’m comfortable with Security approval.

Aisha
Security Approver
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, Jan 17, 2025 at 3:27 PM
Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

Conditional approval from Security to proceed, pending verification of the below in the final PRs/spec:

Approval checklist
1) No default config-file secret discovery. If supported at all, must be explicit opt-in and clearly documented as such.
2) Canonical env var in docs + errors: REDWOOD_API_KEY only.
3) Redaction:
   - Authorization header always redacted
   - Any header name containing token/key/authorization (case-insensitive) redacted
   - Applies to thrown exceptions, debug logs, and telemetry hooks
4) Debug logging off by default in all SDKs.
5) Add tests demonstrating no secret leakage:
   - Unit test per SDK
   - Conformance scenario for “error contains sanitized headers only”

Follow-ups (not blockers for merge, but please track):
- Update docs to include an explicit “Do not log API keys” note and a short multi-tenant guidance section.
- If we add request-id logging hooks, they must not include headers by default.

Please tag me on the PR(s) once the changes are in so we can do a quick final glance.

Naomi

Subject: Re: Security review: SDK auth handling + log redaction (parity audit)

Thanks Naomi/Aisha/Kevin.

We incorporated the checklist into the spec and cut a small set of implementation tasks per SDK:
- Removed config file lookup from default path (and we’re punting optional support to a later iteration)
- REDWOOD_API_KEY is now the only env var name referenced in docs/errors
- Added redactSecrets() helper in each SDK + applied to debug/telemetry/error objects
- Added leak tests (unit + conformance scenario)

I’ll tag you on the updated PRs once they’re up (likely tomorrow morning after CI).

Ibrahim
